reviews.title: The first win happened the same night.
reviews.body: This is what I wish discharge instructions had been: one house rule, one routine, one card for when it looks wrong.
reviews.name: Kemi

reviews.title: The fairness ledger changed everything.
reviews.body: The system is solid. It gave us a clear next step. We finally had a default that worked even when exhausted.
reviews.name: Grace

reviews.title: Works if your partner actually signs.
reviews.body: Every Night, Just Me is practical. It replaces asking with a pre-agreed default. We hit the bad-night protocol twice and having a reset instead of a meltdown — mine — is the part I did not know I needed.
reviews.name: Sade

reviews.title: From chaos to a fridge chart we both follow.
reviews.body: We went from Googling at 3am to checking one chart on the fridge. Both adults see it, both follow it. The argument stopped before it started.
reviews.name: Ife

reviews.title: A real plan for a real situation.
reviews.body: Short, clear, and made for people running on no sleep. We did the first win the same evening we opened it.
reviews.name: Hauwa

reviews.title: This is what I wish the hospital gave us.
reviews.body: We spent months negotiating every night and blaming each other. Every Night, Just Me ended the negotiation. It is not magic — some nights are still hard — but nobody has to ask, and that was the whole problem.
reviews.name: Ada

reviews.title: The re-entry protocol saved us.
reviews.body: What I needed was not more information. I needed a default that holds when we are tired — and a way to recover after a bad night without guilt. This gave us both.
reviews.name: Chiamaka

reviews.title: The roster ended the 3am negotiation.
reviews.body: My mother-in-law kept wanting to rub things on the stump. The family script let me hold the rule without a fight. That alone was worth it.
